alerts.title: EFV neuropsychiatric toxicity causing insomnia and vivid dreams
alerts.message: Guidelines state EFV frequently causes neuropsychiatric effects including insomnia, vivid dreams, and dizziness, typically within the first 2-6 weeks of therapy. This patient started EFV in February 2024 and now reports poor sleep and vivid dreams for several weeks. Evidence for drug attribution: symptoms match the classic EFV neuropsychiatric profile. Evidence against: onset is unusually late (nearly 2 years after initiation), so other causes such as anxiety, depression, or substance use should be excluded. The guideline lists persistent CNS toxicity or mental symptoms as a major adverse event warranting regimen substitution.

evidence.recommended_action: Assess for alternative causes; if symptoms persist or are intolerable, substitute EFV per guideline (e.g., switch to an alternative third agent).

alerts.title: Neuropsychiatric symptoms not documented on aDSM screening form
alerts.message: Guidelines require asking patients about neuropsychiatric symptoms (bad dreams, suicidal thoughts, insomnia, headaches, anxiety, mood changes) at every monthly visit for EFV-containing regimens, and completing the adverse drug reaction (aDSM) form for reporting. This patient's insomnia and vivid dreams were noted in the assessment but no aDSM screening documentation or adverse event reporting appears in the record. Formal screening would also systematically cover suicidal ideation, which was only informally assessed today.

evidence.recommended_action: Complete the aDSM symptom checklist and submit the suspected ADR reporting form for this EFV-related neuropsychiatric event.

alerts.title: No structured mental health or suicidality assessment documented
alerts.message: Guidelines note that suicidality remains a common concern and may require additional assessment, and recommend validated brief instruments such as the PHQ-2/PHQ-9, GAD-7, K-10, or AUDIT for diagnosing depression, anxiety, and substance use. This patient reports persistent insomnia with vivid dreams on EFV, and suicidality was only addressed with a single negative statement without any structured screening tool or documented mental health evaluation. Given EFV's association with depression and anxiety, a structured assessment is warranted.

evidence.recommended_action: Administer a validated screening instrument (e.g., PHQ-9, GAD-7) and perform formal suicidality assessment at this visit.
